resolvedFindings: The first review found that the fixture guard could hide callbacks from disabled controls. Every invocation is now recorded before the state guard, so either additional rendered touch would fail the exact single-open assertion.
The first review found that progress identity was claimed but not observed. The common row now exposes a stable target-scoped progress tag and the test requires it only on the initiating peer.
review.scopeLimit: Hermetic rendered common Compose interaction executed in Web/Wasm; existing native platform and backend race evidence remain separately authoritative.

notes: The rendered common Compose list starts with two independently enabled peer Chat controls. The first touch records one target and immediately disables both the initiating control and its sibling while retaining progress identity on the initiating row.

Additional real touch input delivered to both disabled rendered controls produces no second callback. This closes the presentation gap left by the existing model-level stale-completion and backend pair-convergence evidence.

Android, Web/Wasm and iOS consume ProfileUsersListCommon. The new evidence executes that common component in Chrome Headless and compiles its Android consumer; existing platform E2E remains authoritative and was not repeated solely for this test-only addition.
Backend convergence remains bounded to the separately accepted two-actor same-pair race; broader load and multi-pair concurrency remain outside this presentation-only unit.
